chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Meeting Sid Catlett in the early 1930s and their friendship
summary: Crawford says he met Catlett when he first came to New York and they were jovial friends.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: But now when -- now, what -- do you remember what year it was you met Sid Catlett?
No, I don't offhand. But it was when I first came to New York.
In the early '30s when you first arrived -- '33, '34, right in there?
Yeah, around in there. He was a great drummer.
But you were impressed by his speed? Is that what it was that impressed you?
His speed and his way of thinking, of applying himself and his rhythm. He was always happy and
jovial. Big Sid was laughing all the time. Yeah, I loved Big Sid. He passed also.
Did you -- were you and he very good friends?
Yeah. Sid was a friend of most people, drummers and whatnot. Sid -- people wanted to be friends of his, period. Yes, we were good friends. Big Sid Catlett.
What did you all do together? I mean did you -- when you got together, what kind of things did you do?
Nothing, just -- not even talk drums, talk about women or something like that, have a drink together. Of course, he was just a jovial person. Just like Louis Armstrong.
